feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant technical depth. It reads professionally and is rich in scope, but it would be more impactful with tighter structure, fewer repeated themes, and more outcome-driven achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong public-sector digital leadership profile.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement signals trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve readability and save space.  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: several bullets say “led,” “built,” or “strengthened” without showing measurable outcomes (engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency: use parallel punctuation in lists and bullets; “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; consider standardizing title case and date formatting (“Sept.” vs “Mar.”/“Oct.”). No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and sharpen the opening: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience…” reads more directly than “Senior digital leader.”
- Add a scale marker from recent roles to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal platform,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace the broad list with a more integrated value statement: connect modernization, governance, analytics, and AI to outcomes like usability, coordination, and discoverability.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled discovery for mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal ecosystem serving 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies/footer; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled discovery.”
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating “senior leader” language.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic differentiators rather than repeating broad capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper phrases and align wording with the “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” positioning.
- Prioritize the most distinctive strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Consider replacing broader items with more senior-level language:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and structured content systems • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of “&” if that is the CV-wide preference.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” duplicates the header and Topline Skills; consider removing or reframing.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well covered in the header and experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats several points already covered in Work Experience. Tightening wording and emphasizing outcomes or scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a simple intro line and make formatting consistent: “Recent Projects:” followed by 4 concise bullets.
- Shorten each item to one line with stronger verbs and clearer specificity, e.g. “Created AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace generic phrases like “improve discovery” or “designed for continued campaign growth” with concrete outcomes, audience, or scale if available.
- Standardize style: use parallel verb forms, consistent punctuation, and spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner prose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo role bullets.
- Anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator here because it adds unique cross-channel/event work not stated elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, recent strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named deliverables.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise the National Association of Counties on digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations for enterprise public-facing platforms.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points focused on consulting impact: strategy/governance, Drupal campaign builds, analytics/workflows, AI search initiative.
- Replace generic phrasing like “build and refine” / “advise on” / “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs: “designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “defined.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, workflow time reduced, publishers supported, engagement gains, search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats website, governance, analytics, and multi-channel operations already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be stronger if the opening were tighter, bullets started with outcomes, and channel-management language were less repetitive with the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget strategy for a national association serving county officials.”
- Tighten bullets around biggest wins: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-based: add email open/click growth, social engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; emphasize enterprise leadership, modernization and infrastructure here instead.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo roles; focus this item on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Make it tighter, emphasize what expanded under your leadership, and add any measurable growth if available.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around program-building: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; in this entry, stress expansion/ownership rather than initial creation.
- “Web, email, social and video” also appears in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating channel lists unless paired with a distinct achievement.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, outcome-oriented language tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered advocacy and member communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and publishing standards” or “Cross-functional editorial planning” to better reflect seniority.
- Keep wording parallel and specific; avoid vague labels like “messaging” unless paired with audience or channel context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use only one version across the CV.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep only the most marketable/recent platforms; consider dropping WordPress or SharePoint here if they are not central to recent work.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and discovery” for cleaner phrasing and stronger strategic tone.
- If space allows, make modernization more outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and migration” to align with the 10,000+ page Drupal project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating full platform/tool inventories in both places.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here and move the full stack detail to Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity; KPI design, executive reporting, SEO and performance analysis.”
- If space allows, sharpen impact: “Analytics strategy & optimization — built reporting frameworks and insight workflows using GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” would be stronger and more standard as “executive reporting” or “stakeholder reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a stronger, less junior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production.”
- Consider adding scale or context if space allows: “for advocacy, conferences and recurring digital programming.”
- Keep to 4 concise phrases max; avoid mixing tools, formats, and environments in uneven detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use this section to add specificity, not repeat the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and event production are already supported by recent NACo bullets, so this line should complement those entries rather than restate them.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add specificity (depth/recent use) or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content platforms, migrations, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add a brief qualifier since it is the strongest, most recent platform across current and recent roles.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint; consider keeping platforms here and removing them from the topline section.
- GitHub Pages is the least evidenced platform in the experience section; remove it if space is tight or if it can’t be supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something tighter and more senior: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Deployment.”
- Reorder by relevance/recency and group logically: “JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3.”
- If accurate, add scope/strength via a qualifier: “JavaScript/jQuery for CMS customization” or “API integrations and lightweight serverless automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section more tool-specific.
- GTM may fit better under analytics/measurement if that section needs more depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture strength. Since the CV already emphasizes systems-building in recent NACo roles, this item should be tighter and more purpose-led.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were used to build operational systems, consider replacing the list with: **Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier for workflow automation; Jira, Asana, and Trello for editorial/project operations; Slack and Microsoft Teams for cross-team coordination**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common tools; keep them only if space allows or if central to your workflow leadership.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize email leadership and systems design, this item should signal level of use and strategic relevance, not just names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience engagement)**
- If accurate, add stronger qualifiers tied to recent work: **enterprise email campaigns**, **segmentation/personalization**, **journey automation**, or **member communications**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it for concision

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets already showing email/newsletter leadership; avoid repeating outcomes here
- “Engagement Systems” is somewhat vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications” language elsewhere

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it more technical and execution-focused, not another summary of analytics capability.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as stack + methods: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with stronger phrasing like “reporting dashboards” or “executive reporting” only if that wording is not already emphasized elsewhere.
- Consider “Experimentation” instead of “A/B testing” if formal testing was limited; keep “A/B testing” only if you can support it with examples/results.
- If space allows, order by depth/relevance: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO analysis • Experimentation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one section or making this one purely tools.
- “SEO” and “dashboarding” are broad and may repeat claims already implied by analytics infrastructure in recent NACo roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten and specify outputs: mention website refresh, livestream/event production, weekly video series, and cross-channel publishing support in one concise sentence.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/events, video cadence, audience growth, email/social volume, or size/timeline of the website refresh.
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; use “helped establish” or “supported” here instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work at NACo. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership, especially the podcast launch, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Recast to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated research and innovation projects supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead achievement and use stronger verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer outcome-oriented line such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy initiatives.”
- If possible, add one metric or output count: number of episodes, audience growth, projects supported, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/innovation support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger management evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to software/tools only, and let recent experience entries carry the production/studio impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software & Audio/Video Tools**
- Replace with a cleaner tools-first list: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- If you want one capability phrase, keep it specific and technical: **Livestream production systems** or **Podcast editing**, not both broad workflow terms.
